matchups.analysis: Both teams are sitting at 0.0 with ESPN calling this basically a coin flip at 49-51, but espnfan7338848211's getting the microscopic edge at 124.4 projected versus Doakes22's 122.1—close enough that this is pure execution with nine starters still left on each side. Doakes22's got the safer floor with Justin Jefferson, Saquon Barkley, and Lamar Jackson all likely to produce, while espnfan7338848211's leaning on Ja'Marr Chase and D'Andre Swift to carry the load, so whoever's skill position guys actually show up wins this. Neither one made any real lineup fuck-ups to hand this away, so this is pure roster strength, and honestly it's genuinely too close to call—ESPN's basically saying flip a coin and hope your guys don't collectively tank in the second half. The 1% edge espnfan7338848211's got is basically meaningless with this many unknowns still in play, but if one of these rosters decides to implode, that tiny projection gap becomes a huge psychological advantage heading into Monday.

SteelerFan9828's sitting at 114.6 projected with a 46% win probability while 82Cole47's at 123.6 with 54%, so ESPN's basically saying Cole's got the better roster and the better path here—but both of you still have nine starters left, so this thing isn't decided yet. SteelerFan's got some legit weapons in Amon-Ra, Breece Hall, and Joe Burrow that could absolutely chip away at that gap, but Cole's got a cleaner offensive setup with Josh Allen, Jahmyr Gibbs, and Marvin Harrison Jr. all likely to produce at a higher floor. The real difference is Cole's got more certainty in his remaining lineup—Allen and Gibbs are basically getting fed targets and carries—while SteelerFan's gambling on a few guys needing to pop off to make up that 9-point projection deficit. Cole should probably win this, but if SteelerFan's skill guys actually show up and Cole's offense decides to be mid, this flips real fast.
